title: Merge Two Sorted String Arrays
statement:
You are given two arrays of words, `A` and `B`. Each array is already sorted in **non-decreasing dictionary order** (compare words character by character; a word that is a proper prefix of another comes first).

Merge them into a single array of `n + m` words that is also sorted in non-decreasing dictionary order, and print it. Words that appear in both arrays (or several times) are all kept; equal words are interchangeable, so the printed text is unique.

An array may be empty.
input_format:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `m`, the sizes of `A` and `B`.
The next `n` whitespace-separated tokens are the words of `A`, followed by `m` tokens for the words of `B`. (They are normally given on two lines; a line is empty when its array is empty.)
output_format: Print the merged array as `n + m` space-separated words on one line.
constraints: every word has 1 to 8 lowercase English letters
A and B are each sorted in non-decreasing dictionary order

examples.explanation: Compare the fronts: good < he, so good goes first. Then person > he, so he goes next, then person > is so is goes, and finally person is appended.
All three copies of dog are kept and stay together, after cat and before emu.
A is empty, so the result is just B.

hints: Both inputs are already sorted, so the smallest unused word is always at the front of one of the two arrays.
Keep one pointer into each array. Repeatedly copy the smaller of the two current words and advance that pointer.
When one array runs out, append the remainder of the other. Do not re-sort the combined array: that ignores the sortedness and costs O((n + m) log(n + m)).
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n, m = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    a = data[2:2 + n]
    b = data[2 + n:2 + n + m]
    i = j = 0
    out = []
    while i < n and j < m:
        if a[i] <= b[j]:
            out.append(a[i]); i += 1
        else:
            out.append(b[j]); j += 1
    out.extend(a[i:])
    out.extend(b[j:])
    print(' '.join(out))

main()

import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n, m = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
words = data[2:2 + n + m]
# insertion sort
res = []
for w in words:
    k = len(res)
    while k > 0 and res[k - 1] > w:
        k -= 1
    res.insert(k, w)
print(' '.join(res))
